chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ahmad ibn Idris said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Imran al-Ash'ari narrated, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Ishaq, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Yahya, on the authority of his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, on the authority of Abi Basir, on the authority of Abi Abdillah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his forefathers, on the authority of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon them), who said:
Avoid phlebotomy and depilation on Wednesday, for Wednesday is a day of continuous bad omen, and in it Hell was created.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Wednesday in Shia tradition regarding health and omens?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this chain linking back to Imam Ali (AS), reflecting the Shia tradition of *takhassus* (specific attributes) for days of the week, where Wednesday is viewed as a day of continuous misfortune due to the creation of Hell. This practice of avoiding specific medical or grooming procedures like cupping (*hijama*) and depilation (*nawra*) on this day underscores the intersection of spiritual caution and physical well-being in Shia jurisprudence.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 7-77 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ahmad ibn Idris quoted Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash’ari, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, on the authority of his grandfather Al-Hassan ibn Rashid, on the authority of Abi Basir, on the authority of Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB), on the authority of his father (MGB), on the authority of his forefathers (MGB), on the authority of the Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali (MGB), “
Do not perform phlebotomy or depilatory on Wednesdays since Wednesdays are always with bad omen. Hell was created on a Wednesday.”
